clue.text: Relax in a railway jacket

indicators.note: in tells us the word for relax sits inside the letters for the railway

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the old UK national railway
to laze is to relax idly

explanation.surface: Someone unwinding in a railway jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a railway' is BR, short for British Rail, the old UK state railway; 'jacket' is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a type of tailored sports coat, often worn with a club or school badge.

clue.text: On them one's destitute and smile goes

parts.note: to beam is to smile broadly
ends means finishes or goes, as a road ends or goes no further

explanation.surface: A destitute person's smile fades away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On one's beam ends' is an idiom for being penniless; the definition is phrased so it reads in front of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'on one's beam ends' comes from a ship lying on its side, and means having no money left.

clue.text: There's a world of difference between these places

definitions.text: There's a world of difference between these places

parts.words: There's a world of difference between these places
parts.note: the phrase 'a world of difference' is read literally: these places lie on opposite sides of the globe

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a big contrast is taken literally: the places are diametrically opposite on the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names points on the globe directly opposite each other, commonly Australia and New Zealand from a British view.

clue.text: Bird of another nest

indicators.note: of here means the bird is taken out of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A bird from another bird's nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' signals that the bird comes from inside 'anothER NEst'.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: I'm drunk — spree's so riotous

indicators.note: riotous suggests wild disorder, so the letters of the words before are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A reveller admits to being drunk after a wild spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' suggests intoxication but means 'swallowed': the coffee speaks of itself. 'riotous' rearranges SPREESSO.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong small black coffee is something that gets drunk, so it can say of itself that it is drunk.

clue.text: Long for favourites to come up in London

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters of the words for long and favourites are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing
pets are favourites, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A Londoner longs for the favourites in a race to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' turns YEN and PETS together, giving STEPNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepney is a district of the East End of London.

clue.text: Mad hunter above ' danger will do so

definitions.text: Mad hunter above ' danger will do so

indicators.note: in a down clue above places the first piece over the second
mad means crazed or disordered, so the letters of hunter are scrambled

parts.note: risk means danger

explanation.surface: A reckless hunter goes out looking for danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges HUNTER into RUNTHE; 'above' puts it over RISK. The whole clue is also the definition: a mad hunter will take chances.
explanation.definitionFit: To run the risk is to expose oneself to danger, which a crazy hunter would do.

clue.text: Fleet's churchman

definitions.meaning: fleet as an adjective means quick
Jonathan ..., author of Gulliver's Travels, was Dean of St Patrick's in Dublin

explanation.surface: A churchman belonging to a navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' reads as a navy but is the adjective meaning fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick-moving is the adjective sense; the cleric sense is the satirist Jonathan Swift, an Anglican dean.

clue.text: Gas burner

parts.note: not a stove part but a gas that makes things burn, since combustion needs it

explanation.walkthrough: A 'gas burner' looks like a cooker ring; here it is a gas that supports burning.
explanation.definitionFit: The element that sustains combustion is the gas without which nothing burns.

clue.text: Not well up in one's home, lacking colour

indicators.note: in places the turned word for unwell inside the word for home

parts.note: a pad is slang for one's flat or home

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for not well reads bottom to top

parts.note: ill means not well

explanation.surface: Someone poorly, laid up at home and looking pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not well up' looks like 'not well informed', but 'up' turns the word for unwell, and 'one's home' is slang for a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid means pale, with the colour drained from the face.

clue.text: You had a late meal, we hear, to reduce! -

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a late meal might be eaten at ten o'clock, so the phrase is 'at ten you ate'

explanation.surface: A dieter is told that eating late at night spoils slimming.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, 'at ten you ate' runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To attenuate is to weaken or make thinner, so to lessen.

clue.text: Loud prying round one

indicators.note: round means the word for prying goes around the numeral

parts.note: nosy means prying
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A loud busybody pokes around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts NOSY around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy and loud are synonyms describing high volume.

clue.text: Observe in glasses, pyrotechnic display

indicators.note: in signals the word sits inside the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Watching a fireworks display through spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into 'glassES PYrotechnic'; 'display' just completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or notice.

clue.text: Medium sort of board

parts.note: medium is a spiritualist, not middling: a board used at seances

explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' reads as middling size but is a spiritualist.
explanation.definitionFit: A planchette is a small heart-shaped board on castors used at seances to spell out messages.

clue.text: Count rails fluttering above man's reception

indicators.note: fluttering suggests things flapping about, so the letters of count rails are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone counts railings that flicker past overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' rearranges COUNTRAILS; 'reception' is hearing, as on a radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultrasonic sound has frequencies beyond the range human ears can pick up.

clue.text: Cheated the minister, a novice — perished outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for perished wraps around the other letters

parts.note: died means perished
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a minister's degree
L for learner, the plate on a novice driver's car

explanation.surface: A clergyman and a beginner were swindled and then died.
explanation.walkthrough: DD (Doctor of Divinity) is the crossword's usual stand-in for a minister, and L for learner is a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Diddled is informal British for swindled or done out of something.

clue.text: Kerry's round — bouncing ball

indicators.note: bouncing suggests jumping about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: Kerry is taken as written
O is a round shape

explanation.surface: In a cricket match, Kerry bowls a ball that bounces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncing' suggests the ball itself, but rearranges KERRY plus O. In cricket a yorker pitches at the batsman's feet, so the surface is a misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A yorker is a cricket delivery aimed to land right at the batsman's feet.

clue.text: Duck under the bed-cover

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck
down means below, beneath

explanation.surface: A duck hides beneath the bedspread.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck sits on top of DOWN, which here means 'under'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt originally filled with the soft feathers of the eider duck.

clue.text: Probe round cracked slate with instrument

indicators.note: round means the word for probe goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: to pry is to probe

indicators.note: cracked suggests broken apart, so the letters of slate are rearranged

explanation.surface: Investigating a broken slate with a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' rearranges the letters of slate to SALTE; 'round' wraps the word for probe around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument, plucked like a zither.

clue.text: Acts appropriately?

parts.note: appropriately is read as 'by appropriating', seizing what belongs to another

explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriately' looks like 'suitably' but is the adverb of 'appropriate', to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize power or property wrongfully, which is appropriating it.

clue.text: Arab race in desert mainly

indicators.note: in means the word race goes inside the shortened desert word
mainly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a desert is a sandy waste: sand

explanation.surface: An Arab racing across the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is not a contest here but the plain word, dropped into most of the word for desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the medieval European name for an Arab or Muslim.

clue.text: It's as well man's into insects

indicators.note: into means the man's name goes inside the word for insects

parts.note: bees are insects
Sid is a man's name; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: It is just as well the man has got in among the insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man's' stands for 'man is', so the man is into, or inside, the insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides and as well both mean in addition, too.

clue.text: Cheese on railway, in short, lacks smoothness

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
Ry is the short form of railway

explanation.surface: Cheese served on a train is rough.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts BRIE above RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Briery describes something full of brambles and thorns, so prickly rather than smooth.

clue.text: Useful for tots

parts.note: tots are sums to be added up, not small children

explanation.walkthrough: 'tots' looks like small children, but a tot is also a sum to be added.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires is a counting aid for doing additions.

clue.text: Animals produce as orchard does

parts.note: bears are animals
fruit is produce, the crop grown

explanation.surface: Wild animals give birth like trees in an orchard yield crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' looks like a verb, but it is the noun FRUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Trees in an orchard yield crops each year, which is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: A novice embraces upset nun? Make nothing of it

indicators.note: embraces means the first pieces wrap around the turned word

parts.note: L for learner, a novice

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so nun is read backwards

explanation.surface: A trainee hugs a distressed nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NUN, which reads the same either way; 'embraces' puts A and L around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to cancel or declare void, reducing something to no effect.

clue.text: Heart of chorale's spoken

indicators.note: heart of means taking letters from the centre of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The core of a hymn is sung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of' takes the inner letters of 'chORALe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written.

clue.text: Employer has heads of Unions so easily reconciled

indicators.note: heads of means taking the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An employer finds the union leaders easy to win over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads of' takes the first letters of 'Unions so easily reconciled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who employs a thing, putting it to use.

clue.text: Clergyman is able to proceed here

parts.note: can means is able
on means forward, as in 'go on' when told to proceed

explanation.surface: A clergyman gets permission to go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to proceed' gives ON as in the command 'go on'; 'here' only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: Rock is something of prime importance (with no hesitation)

indicators.note: with no means the letters for hesitation are taken out

parts.note: a cornerstone is something fundamental
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A rock is a key thing, said without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes ER from CORNERSTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornstone is a mottled red limestone found in sandstone beds.

clue.text: Providing foolish figure to audience is synthetic material

indicators.note: to audience means the words are heard spoken, not read

parts.note: a silly icon is a foolish figure or image

explanation.surface: A ridiculous public figure turns out to be artificial.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, 'silly icon' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicone is a man-made polymer used in sealants and implants.

clue.text: Rent to produce tears when girl's taken in

indicators.note: taken in means the girl's name goes inside the word for weeping

parts.note: to cry is to produce tears
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Paying rent makes a girl weep when she is cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid but is a split or tear; the girl is placed inside the weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranny is a small narrow gap or crack, as a rent is a tear.
